ja218:1.1: Treachery to the treacherous is well thought-out,
ja218:1.2: Fraud to the fraudulent is planted in return,
ja218:1.3: If the mice can devour a ploughshare,
ja218:1.4: Why can a hawk not carry away a boy child?
ja218:2.1: There is fraud upon fraud for the fraudulent one,
ja218:2.2: There is cheating in return for the one who cheats,
ja218:2.3: He must give the ploughshare to the one who lost it,
ja218:2.4: The one who lost his ploughshare must not steal his child.
